standard_prerequisites.name: Retract of a function
standard_prerequisites.statement: g : A -> B is a retract of f : X -> Y when there are s : A -> X, r : X -> A, L : prd a, f(s a) = s'(a), K : prd x, r'(f x) = g(r x), and the coherence data recorded in the author's definition.
standard_prerequisites.use: All these maps and homotopies are used to write phi_b and psi_b at source lines 685-688.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fiber of a map
standard_prerequisites.statement: hfiber g b is the type of pairs (a, g a = b).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type on both sides of the retraction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Omission of contractible components
standard_prerequisites.statement: A sigma type whose first component ranges over a contractible type is equivalent to the fiber of the remaining component.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reformulation applied at source line 696.

core_obligations: Unpack the retraction data and, for each b : B, define phi_b(a,p) := (s a, L(a) `ct` s'(p)) and psi_b(x,q) := (r x, K(x) `ct` r'(q) `ct` R'(b)) (source lines 683-689).
Compute the composite psi_b(phi_b(a,p)) explicitly (source line 690) and state the goal that psi_b is a retraction of phi_b with section as claimed (source lines 691-692).
Reduce the pointwise statement to the case p = refl by reordering the first two Pis and applying the omission-of-contractible-components result (source lines 693-699).
Apply the characterisation of paths in sigma types to split the remaining equality of pairs into two component equalities; the first holds by R(a) : r(s a) = a (source lines 700-701).
Compute the required transport as opp(g(R a)) `ct` K(s a) `ct` r'(L a) `ct` R'(g a) and observe that H(a) supplies exactly that path (source lines 702-704).

proof_roadmap.step: Write down the two maps between the fibers.
State the retraction identity and reduce it to the reflexivity case.
Split into components by the sigma-path characterisation and close with H(a).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.7.3 at source lines 677-680: if g is a retract of f then every fiber of g is a retract of the corresponding fiber of f. The author's proof (source lines 682-705) is an explicit construction whose difficulty is entirely in the coherence data: the two maps between fibers have to be written down using all five pieces of the retraction record (lines 685-688), the retraction identity is then reduced by reordering the Pis and applying the omission-of-contractible-components result to the single case p = refl (lines 693-699), and the remaining obstruction is an equality of pairs that is split by the sigma-path characterisation (line 700) and closed only after computing the transport as opp(g(R a)) `ct` K(s a) `ct` r'(L a) `ct` R'(g a) and matching it against the coherence homotopy H(a) (lines 702-704). The statement mentions none of these components.
